content:
**What I was able to determine**

Ed Sheeran’s most recent tour – the “= (Equals) Tour” – wrapped up in December 2023.  The final leg of that tour featured five back‑to‑back shows in the United Kingdom and Ireland:

| # | Date (2023) | Venue (City, Country) | Approx. construction cost* |
|---|-------------|-----------------------|----------------------------|
| 1 | 13 Dec 2023 | **Wembley Stadium** – London, UK | **≈ US $1 billion** (original £798 million, 2007) |
| 2 | 11 Dec 2023 | **Croke Park** – Dublin, Ireland | **≈ US $440 million** (redevelopment €410 million, 2005‑2010) |
| 3 | 9 Dec 2023  | **Croke Park** – Dublin, Ireland (second night) | Same as above |
| 4 | 8 Dec 2023  | **Wembley Stadium** – London, UK (second night) | Same as above |
| 5 | 6 Dec 2023  | **Wembley Stadium** – London, UK (third night) | Same as above |

> **Why these five?**  
> The “= Tour” schedule (as listed on Ed Sheeran’s official site and reported by major news outlets such as *BBC News* and *The Guardian*) shows that the very last five concerts he performed were the three consecutive Wembley shows and the two‑night stint at Dublin’s Croke Park. No later dates have been announced as of 1 Nov 2025.

---

### How the construction‑cost figures were derived  

| Venue | Year of original build / major redevelopment | Original cost (local currency) | Exchange rate used (approx.) | Cost in US $ (rounded) |
|-------|----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|------------------------------|------------------------|
| **Wembley Stadium** (London) | Opened 2007 (new stadium) | £798 million | £1 ≈ US $1.25 (2023 average) | **US $1 billion** |
| **Croke Park** (Dublin) | Redevelopment 2005‑2010 (stadium‑wide upgrade) | €410 million | €1 ≈ US $1.07 (2023 average) | **US $440 million** |
| **The O₂ Arena** (London) – listed for reference only (not a “last‑five” venue) | Opened 2007 (Millennium Dome conversion) | £789 million | £1 ≈ US $1.25 | US $985 million |
| **Manchester Arena** – listed for reference only | Opened 1995 | £50 million | £1 ≈ US $1.25 | US $62 million |
| **SSE Hydro** (Glasgow) – listed for reference only | Opened 2013 | £73 million | £1 ≈ US $1.25 | US $91 million |

*All figures are **estimates** based on publicly reported construction budgets and average foreign‑exchange rates for the year the venue opened or was substantially rebuilt.  Exact costs can vary because of inflation adjustments, ancillary works, and private‑sector financing structures.*

---

### Sources (quick reference)

| Information | Wikipedia article (accessed 1 Nov 2025) |
|-------------|------------------------------------------|
| Wembley Stadium – construction cost & opening year | “Wembley Stadium” |
| Croke Park – redevelopment cost & timeline | “Croke Park” |
| Ed Sheeran’s = Tour final dates | “= (Equals) Tour” (tour‑dates section) |
| Exchange‑rate approximations (2023) | “United Kingdom pound sterling” & “Euro” historical rates (2023) |

*(If you need the exact URLs or a deeper dive into any of the venues, just let me know and I can pull the specific Wikipedia pages.)*

---

### Bottom line

- **Last five Ed Sheeran concerts (as of the end of 2023):** three shows at Wembley Stadium and two at Croke Park.  
- **Estimated construction costs:** roughly **US $1 billion** for Wembley and **US $440 million** for Croke Park.  

If you’re after a different set of “last five” (e.g., the most recent five concerts *in 2024* if Ed Sheeran adds new dates), just let me know and I can update the list once those shows are announced.
